correctness.rationale: The 16 edge patterns are summed symbolically for each dihedrally invariant disagreement projector; the exact 2x2 covariance-action matrix is nonnegative and strictly positive for 0<p<1 and h>0. Perron-Frobenius gives the exact infinite-round squared-disagreement exponent, not merely a one-step bound. Similarity to a symmetric matrix with positive-definite quadratic gain coefficient proves strict convexity and a unique minimizer. Differentiation at the gain constraint h=1/2 and an exact factorization isolate the unique admissible threshold (4-sqrt(5))/11. At p=1 a deterministic mode comparison gives h=1/3. The embedded SymPy checker verified the matrices, eigenvalue discriminant, threshold identity and examples; the proof establishes all p and all rounds.

originality.rationale: The nearest original covariance paper (Patterson et al. 2010) treats general iid random-link consensus and proves the covariance-operator spectral-radius criterion; it does not derive the C4 closed Perron law or the exact constrained-gain threshold. The 2023 paper treats random-subgraph distributed Kalman filtering with sufficient gain bounds. Closest published network-mixing records concern deterministic gains, graph structures or distinct objectives. Because the general operator is an especially close precursor and historical search cannot be exhaustive, priority is provisional.
residual_risks: The 2010 operator model already covers covariance evolution generally; the new closed-form minimax switching threshold is a specialization derived here and could conceivably have been obtained elsewhere.

value.rationale: C4 is the smallest regular simple cycle exhibiting a genuine disagreement-mode split. The exact optimization of the true asymptotic covariance spectral radius is a practical contrast to one-step tuning: independent missing links create a sharp regime where maximal stochastic gain is optimal, followed by a regime where a unique interior gain is faster. The result includes a reproducible nontrivial exact threshold and complete classification at both endpoints; at p=1/2 it improves the asymptotic rate from 0.5 at h=1/2 to approximately 0.47935743 at h=0.43575315. It is a deliberately limited complete result for a natural minimal network, not an assertion about all graphs.
